1.stem_plain: "We'd be going out for dinner, _________ we?" asked Mother.

2.stem_plain: The number of Covid-19 cases _________ on the decline since we have enforced stricter measures.

3.stem_plain: The person _________ the dog barked at is my new neighbour.

4.stem_plain: We will not get to the peak of the mountain before sunset _________ we hurry up.

5.stem_plain: David took Susan's school bag home by mistake as he thought it was _________.

6.stem_plain: We can get to the airport quickly _________ car.

7.stem_plain: Joe's pet turtle went missing _________ his negligence.

8.stem_plain: Since we started the Reduce, Reuse and Recycle campaign in school, we have generated _________ waste.

9.stem_plain: The helpless victim could only watch the robber _________ her handbag.

10.stem_plain: The boys _________ on the computer for hours before their parents turned off the computers.

1.zh: “我们会出去吃晚饭，不是吗？”妈妈问。
1.note: 附加问句 (Question tag)：陈述为 would 肯定式，附加部分用 wouldn't + 主语。时态与情态动词一致。

2.concept: 主谓一致 — Subject–verb agreement (number of)
2.zh: 自我们实施更严格措施以来，新冠病例数量一直在下降。
2.note: 主谓一致：the number of + 复数名词仍用单数谓语；since 引导时间，常用现在完成进行或一般现在表趋势。

3.zh: 狗对着吠叫的那个人是我的新邻居。
3.note: 定语从句 (Relative clause)：介词 at 的宾语指人时用 whom（正式书面）。

4.zh: 除非我们加快速度，否则日落前到不了山顶。
4.note: 条件句：unless = 如果不……就不……；与否定主句搭配表必要条件。

5.zh: 大卫误把苏珊的书包带回家，以为那是自己的。
5.note: 物主代词：his/her 后不接名词；hers/mine 单独作表语。

6.zh: 我们坐车可以很快到机场。
6.note: 介词短语作状语：表示交通方式用 by + 交通工具（无冠词）。

7.zh: 乔的宠物龟因他的疏忽而走失了。
7.note: 因果：owing to / due to + 名词表原因；in spite of 表让步。

8.zh: 自从学校开展减废活动，我们产生的垃圾更少了。
8.note: 数量词：less + 不可数；fewer + 可数复数。

9.concept: 不定式 — Perception verb + bare infinitive
9.zh: 无助的受害者只能眼睁睁看着劫匪抢走她的手提包。
9.note: 感官/观察动词后接宾语 + 动词原形（bare infinitive）。

10.concept: 过去完成时 — Past perfect continuous
10.zh: 父母关掉电脑前，男孩们已在电脑上玩了好几个小时。
10.note: 过去完成进行 (Past perfect continuous)：强调在过去另一动作之前持续的进行状态。

11.stem_plain: Sophia had no _________ to her own house as she had left her keys in the office.

12.stem_plain: Several of the customers have made a/an _________ against Mr Lee's restaurant for selling unhygienic food.

13.stem_plain: Mary _________ her chance to win in the story-telling competition because she was too nervous on stage.

14.stem_plain: The teacher constantly say words of encouragement to _________ her pupils' morale after they did not do well for mid-year examinations.

15.stem_plain: Mr Lim was upset when he received a _________ salary despite working long hours.

11.zh: 索菲亚进不了自己家，因为把钥匙落在办公室了。
11.note: 选1：access to 固定搭配表“进入/使用某处”。avenue 多指街道；entrance 指物理门口；admission 偏门票/录取。
11.concept: 词汇辨析 — access（进入权；使用权）

choices.zh: 进入权，使用权；接触机会（名词，指能够进入某个地点、使用某种资源、读取特定数据或与某人接触的权利、机会或手段）
choices.eg: Sophia had no access to her own house as she had left her keys in the office after the late-night meeting.

choices.zh: 林荫大道，大街；途径，渠道（名词，物理上指两旁有树木的宽阔街道，抽象上指达到某种目的、解决某种问题的可行途径或方式）
choices.eg: The National Day parade moved slowly along the tree-lined avenue while thousands of spectators cheered from the sidewalks.

choices.zh: 入口，大门口；进入，登场（名词，指进入建筑物、房间或某个封闭区域的具体物理通道或门，亦指人或演员进入某处的动作）
choices.eg: A guard stood by the side entrance to check our security passes before letting us enter the government building.

choices.zh: 准许进入，入场费；录取，入场券（名词，指官方允许某人进入学校、机构、剧场或景点的正式许可，也可指进入时收取的门票费用）
choices.eg: Admission to the art museum is free on public holidays, drawing large crowds of families and tourists.

12.zh: 几位顾客就李先生餐馆出售不卫生食品提出指控。
12.note: 选3：make an accusation against 控告。protest/object 语气较弱；conspiracy 语义不符。
12.concept: 词汇辨析 — accusation（指控；控告）

choices.zh: 抗议，反对行动（名词，指公众或群体对某项政策、法律或决定表示强烈不满、公开反对而组织的集会、游行或抗议活动）
choices.eg: Residents organised a peaceful protest against the new parking charges to show their deep dissatisfaction to the local council.

choices.zh: 反对，反对意见（名词，指对某人的观点、计划、法庭提问或决定表示不赞同、提出质疑或反驳的正式意见和声明）
choices.eg: The judge sustained the lawyer's objection to the unfair question and instructed the witness not to provide an answer.

choices.zh: 指控，控告（名词，指在没有最终判决前，公开谴责、举报或正式控诉某人犯有某种罪行、过错或不道德行为）
choices.eg: Several customers made an accusation against Mr Lee's restaurant for selling unhygienic food, leading to an immediate health inspection.

choices.zh: 阴谋，密谋（名词，指两人或多人为了达到非法、不道德或不可告人的目的，而在暗中秘密策划、共同实施的恶劣计划）
choices.eg: Detectives successfully broke up a sinister conspiracy to cheat elderly shoppers out of their lifetime retirement savings.

13.zh: 玛丽因在台上太紧张而浪费了赢得讲故事比赛的机会。
13.note: 选4：throw away a chance 浪费机会。throw in 投降；throw off 摆脱；throw out 扔出。
13.concept: 词汇辨析 — threw away（浪费；抛弃（机会））

choices.zh: 放弃，作为赠品附送（短语动词，多用于习语 throw in the towel 表示认输、放弃，或在买卖中指额外免费赠送某物）
choices.eg: After two severe losses, the head coach threw in the towel and rested all the injured players for the remaining season.

choices.zh: 摆脱，甩掉（疾病或追捕者）（短语动词，指身体从感冒、发烧等小病中康复过来，或成功逃脱、甩开跟踪自己的人）
choices.eg: She managed to throw off her nasty cold just in time to participate in the national speech competition.

choices.zh: 驱逐，把……赶出去；扔掉（短语动词，指官方人员强行将不守规矩的人赶出场馆，或指拒绝、废除某项不实建议与计划）
choices.eg: The strict theater usher threw out anyone who tried to enter the main performance hall without a valid security ticket.

choices.zh: 白白浪费，轻易抛弃（机会、优势）（短语动词，指由于自身失误、大意或心理素质不佳，而白白错失了极好的发展机遇或获胜机会）
choices.eg: Mary threw away her chance to win in the story-telling competition because she was too nervous on stage and forgot her lines.

14.zh: 老师不断用鼓励的话来提升学生的士气。
14.note: 选2：boost morale 提振士气。bond 联结；boast 自夸；benefit 受益（不及物搭配不同）。
14.concept: 词汇辨析 — boost（提高；鼓舞）

choices.zh: 建立联系，培养感情；黏合（动词，指通过共同的经历、兴趣在人与人之间建立起深厚的信任和亲密关系，或指物体牢固地结合在一起）
choices.eg: The overnight leadership camp helped the new secondary school pupils bond with one another through exciting team-building games.

choices.zh: 提高，推动，鼓舞（动词，指给某事物带来积极的推动力，使其在数量、水平、信心或士气上得到显著的提升或改善）
choices.eg: The English teacher's warm praise helped boost the class morale significantly after they received the poor vocabulary test results.

choices.zh: 自夸，吹嘘（动词，指带着骄傲、自满的情绪，向他人过度夸耀自己的成就、财富、社会地位或拥有的优越条件）
choices.eg: He tends to boast about his school grades whenever relatives visit their house, making his siblings feel highly uncomfortable.

choices.zh: 使受益，对……有益（动词，指某种行为、物质、政策或环境能够给某人的身体健康、生活水平或学业发展带来实质性的好处）
choices.eg: Developing good reading habits and eating more vegetables can benefit your health and academic performance in the long run.

15.zh: 林先生工作时间长，薪水却很少，因此很沮丧。
15.note: 选3：meagre salary 微薄薪水。mere 仅强调“只不过”；scarce 偏稀缺；sufficient 与 upset 矛盾。
15.concept: 词汇辨析 — meagre（微薄的；少得可怜的）

choices.zh: 仅仅的，只不过的（形容词，常用来强调某物非常小、非常少或微不足道，纯粹用于突出程度之低或数量之少）
choices.eg: After all that intensive work, his reward was a mere five dollars, which barely covered his transport expenses.

choices.zh: 稀缺的，缺乏的（形容词，常指因为环境变化、供求失衡而导致生活必需品、资源或食物在某地变得很难找到、数量极少）
choices.eg: Fresh drinking water became scarce in the village during the prolonged summer drought, causing great worry among residents.

choices.zh: 微薄的，贫乏的，少得可怜的（形容词，特指薪水、食物、收入或分量极其微少，难以维持生计或完全不满足正常需求）
choices.eg: Mr Lim was deeply upset when he received a meagre salary at the end of the month despite working long hours at the factory.

choices.zh: 充足的，足够的（形容词，指某物的数量、质量或条件在客观上已经完全能够满足特定需求，不需要再额外补充）
choices.eg: The total supply of medical masks was sufficient for every student in the secondary school to change theirs daily.

cloze: Leia was stuck at home because of bad weather. She [Q16 (deliberated over)] the options she had. She could do nothing but watch television. She knew that it was a waste of time and her elder sister, Rosie, would [Q17 (frown upon)] her decision. Unlike her, Rosie was a go-getter. [Q18 (Like clockwork)], Rosie would be up by six every morning to go for her run before she worked on her to-do lists. Leia respected Rosie as she was [Q19 (steadfast)] in her belief that being responsible is the key to success. With that in mind, Leia forced herself to get up from the couch and do push-ups. Soon, she was sweating and felt refreshed [Q20 (instantly)]. After that, Leia started working on her project which was due next week.
zh: Leia 因坏天气困在家里。她仔细权衡自己有哪些选择。她似乎只能看电视打发时间。她知道那是浪费时间，姐姐 Rosie 也会不赞成她的决定。和她不同，Rosie 是个积极进取的人。Rosie 每天六点准时起床，先跑步，再处理待办事项。Leia 很佩服 Rosie，因为她坚信负责任是成功的关键。想到这里，Leia 强迫自己从沙发上起来做俯卧撑。很快她就出汗了，并立刻感到精神一振。之后，她开始做下周要交的项目。

16.note: 应选（4）'contemplated'：短文划线的 deliberated over 在此语境下与此义最接近。'decided'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。'wondered'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。'concluded'：义为'断定；得出结论'，与短文语境或搭配要求不一致。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。
16.zh: 她仔细权衡自己有哪些选择。

choices.zh: 决定，下定决心（动词，指在对比各种可能性或经过短暂权衡之后，明确选定一个行动方向或结果）
choices.eg: The committee decided to implement the new environmental policy after reviewing the feedback from the community.

choices.zh: 想知道，琢磨（动词，指内心对某事感到好奇，想了解其真实原因、发展情况或背后隐藏的秘密）
choices.eg: The primary school pupils wondered why the laboratory experiment yielded such an unexpected chemical reaction.

choices.zh: 断定，得出结论（动词，指在仔细检查所有可用的事实、证据、线索或经过深入调查后，做出的最终判定）
choices.eg: After examining the forensic evidence at the crime scene, the detective concluded that the suspect was lying about his whereabouts.

choices.zh: 沉思，仔细考虑，盘算（动词，指花较长时间在脑海中极其严肃、深刻地思考某项决定、计划、选择或未来的发展路线）
choices.eg: The student contemplated several study timetable strategies before committing to her final revision schedule for the exams.

17.concept: 近义词 — frown upon（不赞成）
17.note: 应选（3）'disapprove of'：短文划线的 frown upon 在此语境下与此义最接近。'disregard for'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。'disallow from'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。'disconnect from'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。
17.zh: 她知道那是浪费时间，姐姐 Rosie 也会不赞成她的决定。

choices.zh: 无视
choices.eg: The passage phrase disregard for appears in formal exam English.

choices.zh: 禁止来自
choices.eg: The passage phrase disallow from appears in formal exam English.

choices.zh: 不赞成
choices.eg: The passage phrase disapprove of appears in formal exam English.

choices.zh: 断开连接
choices.eg: The passage phrase disconnect from appears in formal exam English.

18.concept: 近义词 — Like clockwork（照例；常规地）
18.note: 应选（1）'routinely'：短文划线的 Like clockwork 在此语境下与此义最接近。'irregularly'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。'occasionally'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。'sporadically'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。
18.zh: Rosie 每天六点照例起床，先跑步，再处理待办事项。

choices.zh: 照例；常规地
choices.eg: The nurse routinely checks patients' blood pressure.

choices.zh: 不规律地
choices.eg: She answered irregularly before the bell rang.

choices.zh: 偶然地
choices.eg: She answered occasionally before the bell rang.

choices.zh: 零星地
choices.eg: She answered sporadically before the bell rang.

19.note: 应选（4）'unwavering'：短文划线的 steadfast 在此语境下与此义最接近。'unsure'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。'unafraid'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。'unrivalled'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。
19.zh: Leia 很佩服 Rosie，因为她对“负责任是成功的关键”这一信念坚定不移。

choices.zh: 不确定
choices.eg: The speaker chose unsure to match the tone of the passage.

choices.zh: 无所畏惧
choices.eg: The speaker chose unafraid to match the tone of the passage.

choices.zh: 无与伦比的
choices.eg: The coach unrivalled the players after the match.

choices.zh: 坚定不移
choices.eg: The team kept unwavering until the task was done.

20.note: 应选（4）'immediately'：短文划线的 instantly 在此语境下与此义最接近。'hastily'：义为'匆忙地；草率地'，与短文语境或搭配要求不一致。'hurriedly'：与题干语境或搭配要求不一致。'suddenly'：义为'突然地'，与短文语境或搭配要求不一致。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。
20.zh: 很快她就出汗了，并立刻感到精神一振。

choices.zh: 匆忙地；草率地
choices.eg: She hastily packed her bag because the bus was already at the stop.

choices.zh: 慌忙地
choices.eg: She answered hurriedly before the bell rang.

choices.zh: 突然地
choices.eg: She answered suddenly before the bell rang.

choices.zh: 即时地
choices.eg: She answered immediately before the bell rang.

21.stem_plain: In **'Visit the Expo City this June and learn more about endangered animals'**, an asterisk (*) is used to _________.

options.2: relate the point to an explanation
options.3: make a point more visually appealing
options.4: encourage readers to read more carefully

22.stem_plain: According to the flyer, to participate in the poster design competition, Ahmad has to _________.

options.1: start drawing only at twelve noon
options.2: produce a student pass upon registration
options.3: bring his own drawing paper and other art materials
options.4: create a poster related to the dangers faced by all animals

23.stem_plain: Which one of the following statements about the Art Exhibition is true?

options.1: Tickets to the exhibition can be purchased online.
options.2: The exhibition is held throughout the whole month of June.
options.3: A school group can request for a guided tour at the entrance.
options.4: All paintings showcased at the Art Exhibition are by Andy Chua.

24.stem_plain: Bella, a ten-year-old pupil, can only visit the Expo City between 21 and 25 June. She can participate in the _________.

options.3: Art Exhibition and Poster Design Competition
options.4: Poster Design Competition and Figurine-Making Workshop

25.stem_plain: What can a nine-year-old boy do at Expo Hall 3 on 24 June?

options.1: create a small clay figurine of himself
options.2: view the works of a famous local artist
options.3: draw a picture of a red panda on a piece of paper
options.4: make a clay animal together with one of his parents

26.stem_plain: What is a similarity among the activities held at the Expo City?

options.1: They are open to students only.
options.2: They are held on the same day.
options.3: They are organised to educate the public.
options.4: They are free for all student pass holders.

27.stem_plain: Amy wishes to receive stories and news about wildlife regularly. What should she do?

options.1: make a call to Mandy at 6453 6547
options.3: sign up for the Wildlife Foundation membership
options.4: participate in at least one activity at the Expo City

28.stem_plain: What is the main purpose of the flyer?

options.1: to promote the various activities held at the Expo City
options.2: to provide the dates of the Figurine-making Workshops
options.3: to show the admission ticket prices for the Art Exhibition
options.4: to warn that endangered animals are facing extinction soon

21.concept: 题型 — Footnote marker（题型考点）
21.note: Asterisk (*) points readers to a footnote/explanation at the bottom of the flyer.

22.concept: 细节 — Detail check（信息定位）
22.note: Competition rules state participants must bring own drawing paper and art materials.

23.concept: 细节 — Detail check (true)（信息定位）
23.note: Exhibition blurb says paintings are by Andy Chua (local artist).

24.note: Bella (10) available 21–25 June: can do Art Exhibition and Poster Design (workshop dates differ).

25.concept: 题型 — Age + date（题型考点）
25.note: 9-year-old on 24 June at Hall 3: view works of famous local artist (exhibition).

26.concept: 题型 — Main idea（题型考点）
26.note: All activities aim to educate the public about wildlife/conservation.

27.note: Regular wildlife news → sign up for Wildlife Foundation membership.

28.concept: 主旨 — main purpose（主要目的）
28.note: Flyer promotes visiting Expo City in June and learning about endangered animals.

cloze: Small pox was a terrible disease. You would [Q29] high fever, sore throat, headaches, body aches and difficulty breathing. In addition, rashes filled with pus would be all over your body. Even [Q30] the rashes dry out and start falling off, the scars remained.

[Q31] a small pox epidemic in England in 1744, a farmer, Benjamin Jester, decided to scratch some pus from the cowpox sores into the skin of his wife and sons. Surprisingly, none of [Q32] contracted smallpox.

Many years later, Edward Jenner, [Q33] doctor working in the town of Berkeley, decided to try the same approach after gathering evidence from farmers and milkmaids. [Q34] Benjamin did not know the science underlying the discovery, he had actually created the smallpox vaccine. He did not seek to make money from his vaccine as he wanted [Q35] people to get vaccinated. Soon, small pox vaccination was a common practice [Q36] the world and small pox was eradicated in 1979.
[Q37] innovation by Jester and Jenner changed the world and saved millions of lives. What we [Q38] learn from this is not to dismiss bizarre innovations as useless!
zh: 天花是一种可怕的疾病。你会高烧、喉咙痛、头痛、身痛且呼吸困难。此外，全身会出现脓疱。即使皮疹干涸脱落，疤痕仍会留下。
1744年英国天花流行时，农夫 Benjamin Jester 将牛痘脓刮入妻儿皮肤。令人惊讶的是，他们都没有感染天花。
多年后，在 Berkeley 行医的 Edward Jenner 在收集农民与挤奶女工的证据后，尝试同样做法。虽然 Benjamin 不懂其中的科学，他实际上创造了天花疫苗。他不想靠疫苗牟利，希望更多人接种。很快全球普遍接种，天花于1979年被消灭。
Jester 与 Jenner 的创新改变了世界，拯救了数百万人。我们应学到：不要贸然把看似古怪的创新视为无用。

29.note: You would have high fever, sore throat, headaches, = 看前后搭配，选 have。

30.note: Even after the rashes dry out and = 时间/从属 → after。

31.note: during a small pox epidemic in = 时间/从属 → during。

32.note: Surprisingly, none of them contracted smallpox. = 结合句意选 them。

33.note: Many years later, Edward Jenner, a doctor working in the town = 冠词/限定词 a。

34.note: although Benjamin did not know the = 结合句意选 although。

For so long, I have been living in my own [Q39(bliss)] world, thinking no matter how hard things become, they will [Q40(outimately)] get better with you around. Despite the painful memories evoked, you would always [Q45(concluded)] by saying, "The war brought about a generation capable of [Q46(overcame)] all odds." zh: 我从没想到我们会这么快就要说再见。这么久以来，我一直活在自己幸福的小世界里，以为无论事情有多难，有你在身边终会好起来。我实在无法接受自己将要在英国求学四年、会多么想念你。
我最鲜活的记忆是你讲故事时眉头紧锁的样子，你讲述日据时期如何幸存的经历。尽管会唤起痛苦回忆，你总会以一句“战争造就了一代能克服一切困难的人”作结。战时被迫辍学，你加倍努力弥补失去的年月，还为自己赢得了奖学金。
你教会我韧性与勤奋，我也会用功读书来报答你。我爱你，爷爷。

cloze: All of us have our moments when we become angry with someone. [Q51] our fit of anger, we might [Q52] our patience and hurt someone we care about with our words or actions. Even if it is unintentional, the best course of [Q53] is to apologise. However, making an apology is often [Q54] said than done. Thankfully, it can be learned.

First of all, the apology [Q55] be sincere. A half-hearted one could do more damage than none at [Q56]. To show sincerity, you need to take responsibility [Q57] your actions. Find an appropriate time to explain to the other person exactly what happened and how [Q58] you regret it.

After you have said your piece, give that person a chance to speak [Q59] interrupting. You might hear unpleasant things said about you [Q60] of frustration and be tempted to defend [Q61], but what you might not know [Q62] that this is part of the healing process — your active listening recognises the hurt that person is experiencing. It brings about relief and makes it easier for that person to forgive you.
Lastly, you offer to make amends. Actions [Q63] louder than words so if you have damaged someone's property, have it [Q64] or replaced.

Even though an effective and sincere apology can often strengthen a relationship, forgiveness may not necessarily come immediately. You could liken the forgiveness journey [Q65] how a bruise heals — it could take days or even years. What you can do is to keep your heart open for reconciliation one day.
zh: 生气时我们可能会失去耐心，用言语或行为伤害在乎的人；即使无意，最好也去道歉，但道歉往往说来容易做来难，幸好可以学会。
首先道歉必须真诚；敷衍的道歉可能比不道歉更糟。要表现诚意，须为自己的行为负责，找合适时机说明经过并表达悔意。
你说完后给对方说话的机会，不要打断；对方可能因沮丧说难听话，你会想为自己辩护，但倾听是疗愈的一部分，能减轻对方痛苦、更易获得原谅。
最后提出弥补：行动胜于言语；若损坏他人物品，应修理或更换。
真诚道歉常能巩固关系，但原谅未必立刻到来；原谅像淤青愈合，可能需数日甚至数年；你能做的是心怀和解，等待那一天。

51.note: 位于句首且修饰名词短语 our fit of anger（怒火中烧之际）。表示“在……期间/当……的时候”，填入时间介词 In 或者是 During。位于句首需大写。

52.note: 前面有情态动词 might，后面接动词原形。与后面的名词 patience（耐心）组合，在愤怒情绪的语境下，指人们可能会“失去（lose）”耐心并伤害到他人。

53.note: 与其前置的名词短语 the best course of 完美结合。构成全行业、各类日常交流中极其核心和高频的专属行事习语 the best course of action，意为此时最好的“做法/应对行动”。

54.concept: 经典谚语与比较级形式
54.note: 后接比较连词 than done。完美套用英语中家喻户晓的经典处事谚语 easier said than done，意为做出道歉往往是“说起来容易做起来难”。

55.note: 作为主句的谓语。后面接系动词原形 be 极其形容词 sincere，指代道歉“必须（must/should/ought to）”出自真心，用来强调道歉诚意的重要性。

56.note: 与其前置的否定倒装结构 than none at 完美组合。构成高频常考的绝对否定强调习语 none at all，意为半心半意的敷衍道歉比“完全不”道歉带来的伤害还要大。

57.note: 后接名词短语 your actions。构成在各大主流名校考卷中屡次重复考核的核心专属搭配 take responsibility for something，意为必须对自己的所作所为“承担责任”。

58.note: 引导特殊疑问从句。修饰后面的谓语动词 regret（后悔），用以向对方展示你究竟有多么“深地（deeply）”或者是多么“诚恳地/多地（much）”感到追悔莫及。

59.concept: 介词引导条件/状态状语
59.note: 后接动名词形式 interrupting（打断）。指在自己陈述完之后，应当给对方说话的机会而“绝不（without）”能出言干预打断，以此表达对倾听过程的尊重。

60.note: 与后面的名词 frustration（沮丧/挫败感）完美组合。构成形容情绪动因的经典核心短语 out of frustration，意为对方嘴里说出的那些难听话其实只是“出于”一时的宣泄。

61.concept: 反身代词与人称视角一致
61.note: 在主从句中，动作的发起者是第二人称 you（你）。根据主语与宾语为同一人的语法规则，作动词 defend 的宾语，必须填入反身代词 yourself，表示不要急于“为你自己辩护”。

62.concept: 主语从句主系表结构系动词
62.note: 作为由 What you might not know 引导的主语从句后的核心系动词。后接由 that 引导的表语从句。本句陈述客观哲理，指你或许不知道的“是（is）”这恰恰属于治愈过程的一部分。

63.note: 主语为复数名词 Actions（行动）。完美套用英语中关于言行举止最具代表性的核心经典谚语 Actions speak louder than words，意为“事实胜于雄辩/行动胜于言辞”。

64.concept: 使役结构后的过去分词充当宾补
64.note: 前面有经典的使役动词结构 have it...，后接过去分词（V-ed）形式充当宾语补足语，表示动作由别人来完成。指如果弄坏了别人的财产，应当让人把它“修好（repaired/fixed）”或是予以更换。

65.note: 与其前置的动词短语 liken the forgiveness journey 完美组合。构成在各类科学比喻及高级叙事文本里出题率极高、用于打比方的专属经典短语动词 liken A to B，意为将宽恕的历程“比作”伤口的愈合。

paragraphs.1: 卡里姆叹着气，又把身上的钱数了一遍。他仍差五十美元，才买得起那辆最新的 Speedster X 自行车。为了攒零花钱换掉那辆已经嫌小的旧车，过去三个月里他每天都带三明治上学。虽然他瘦了一些，父母并不在意；一位邻居可怜他，每次让他洗车就付他十美元。他把每一分钱都存了起来。
paragraphs.6: “我刚才在隔壁碰见刚搬来的金阿姨。”母亲的声音打断了他的思绪。“她儿子肖恩从下周起要骑车上学。待会儿你能带他走去学校的小路吗？反正是星期六！”
paragraphs.9: 卡里姆哼了一声。他知道自己反抗也没用，母亲大概已经替他在金阿姨面前答应下来了。
paragraphs.11: “对了，你有信。大概是外婆寄来的。拆开看看。”
paragraphs.12: 卡里姆的外婆住在国外，却会不时寄来突然想到就拍的照片和贺卡。他撕开信封，抽出一张贺卡，一张五十美元的钞票滑了出来。他简直不敢相信自己眼前这笔意外之财！
paragraphs.15: “你知道你的名字在阿拉伯语里是‘慷慨’的意思吗？”母亲提醒道，“也许这笔钱能给另一家带来一点快乐。”
paragraphs.17: 卡里姆把钱塞进口袋，哼了一声说：“我这段时间攒得多辛苦，这笔钱我比任何人都更有资格留着。”
paragraphs.19: 下午两点，卡里姆按两位母亲安排，在组屋楼下与肖恩见面。这件差事一办完，他就能越早去自行车店。两个孩子正骑着车，一只松鼠从停着的车后窜出来，猛地冲过马路；两人撞在一起，还撞倒了一些回收箱。
paragraphs.23: “呃！”卡里姆咕哝道，“我忘了提醒你这里松鼠很多。”他把自行车扶起来，肖恩则把箱子摆回去。
paragraphs.25: 砰！两人猛地回头——一辆车急刹在肖恩自行车刚才所在的位置，一个怒气冲冲的男人推开车门。
paragraphs.27: “你撞了我的自行车！”肖恩大喊着跑去捡那一堆扭成一团的零件。
paragraphs.28: “怪你自己！”那人反驳道，一边查看车头，“你把自行车留在路中间。你该庆幸我的车没坏！”他二话没说跳上车扬长而去。
paragraphs.31: “糟了！我本来打算每天骑车上学，帮父母省点钱。”肖恩焦急地说。
paragraphs.33: 卡里姆心想：反正也不是我的错，我还是要买 Speedster X 的；可看着肖恩默默推着残骸回家，一股不安的难过仍哽在喉咙里。
